title: Persist planning authority at proposal
description: OBJECTIVE: make the existing authenticated plan.propose production path persist actual approved-plan and criteria candidate CONTENT instead of dropping it after parsing. HARD DEPENDENCIES: task-b42db644e532413ba2402e7ac40c7146 (daemon planning-authority envelope) and task-ff82bb7580e946c3887b4ee3e05af860 (plan.propose authority carrier) must be DONE and re-measured. DELIVERABLE: the real daemon plan.propose handler builds the canonical envelope from its admitted command, commits it atomically with PlanProposed through SqliteEventStore, and returns/refuses using stable codes and layers. NOT IN SCOPE: approval.decide/current-graph binding, plan/criteria current readers, context selection, or a new wire kind. VERIFICATION: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` must execute with nonzero counts.
definitionOfDone: The real authenticated plan.propose path validates command authority before any durable write and persists one canonical envelope containing the nonempty PlanRevision and AcceptanceContract bodies with the existing planning events/gate.

The PlanProposed event, command decision, receipt, aggregate/version, project/principal/run identity, result bytes, and both body digests are mutually bound; a body/ref/hash mismatch refuses with an exact code/layer before any event or decision residue.

Identical replay returns the original durable envelope and leaves raw event/decision counts unchanged; the same decision identity with conflicting command bytes refuses exactly and preserves the original bytes.

Focused tests use real SqliteEventStore plus the real production handler, include one accepted control and positive-count hostile cases, and assert exact code/layer, zero partial residue on precommit refusals, and nonzero persisted plan steps/criteria obligations.
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` exits 0 with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts, owned production files remain <=250, and no new RuntimeCommandKind or caller-selected approval authority is introduced.
taskRails: Do not start until both named dependencies are DONE; verify the daemon @moe/core manifest, lock importer, and compiled bare-specifier edge before implementation.
Use the existing plan.propose authenticated production edge and its decision identity; never add a test-only put/seed authority.
Commit plan and criteria content in the same durable business effect as PlanProposed so one cannot survive without the other.

(b) Core codecs reachable from the @moe/core ROOT barrel (grep index.ts): encodePlanRevision, decodePlanRevisionBytes, derivePlanRevisionDigest, encodeAcceptanceContract, decodeAcceptanceContractBytes, deriveAcceptanceContractDigest — admitPlanAuthoritySubmission is NOT root-exported, so the builder composes through the body codecs (their encode paths run full admission internally with the body vocabularies' own codes/layers). (c) Dependency-edge rail: worker-21246c33 already verified all three legs (manifest :23, lock importer :123, bare-specifier probe exit 0) — re-run the probe leg only, cheap. implementationPlan.note:
RE-MEASURED under the comment-d10bc0c5 rescope at HEAD d2594cd. The superseded envelope-at-propose premise is NOT retried; comment-4f54a956 stands as the measurement of record for why.

(a) CARRIER, confirmed at HEAD: `propose()` calls `planAuthorityCarry(command, command.submissionHash)` and spreads `...carriedAuthority(carry)` into the sealed event, so `PlanningSubmissionSealed` carries exactly the six identity fields {criteriaDigest, criteriaRef, graphContentHash, graphRevisionRef, planHash, revisionId} and NO bodies. The folded state after a plan.propose chain is lifecycle SUBMISSION_DRAINING with sealedHashes null and graphRevisionRef null — measured by running the reducer, not by reading it. That is the gap this row closes: the bodies are parsed, cross-checked and then dropped.

(b) ROOT BARREL, one hit each in packages/core/src/index.ts: encodePlanRevision, decodePlanRevisionBytes, derivePlanRevisionDigest, encodeAcceptanceContract, decodeAcceptanceContractBytes, deriveAcceptanceContractDigest — plus PLAN_REVISION_LAYERS and ACCEPTANCE_CONTRACT_LAYERS, which step 4 needs to spread into SERVICE_REFUSED_BY. `admitPlanAuthoritySubmission` returns ZERO hits: it is NOT root-exported (deliberately — I left it unpublished when I landed ff82bb75, since the reducer is its in-package consumer). So the builder composes through the BODY codecs, whose encode paths run full admission internally and answer with the body vocabularies' own codes and layers. That is better for this row than the parser would have been: the refusals that travel out are the ones a reader of the durable bytes can reproduce.

(c) DEPENDENCY EDGE, probe leg re-run: a compiled probe importing the BARE specifier `@moe/core` inside apps/daemon typechecks exit 0, deleted in the same command. Manifest :23 and lock importer :123 were verified in the blocked attempt and have not moved.

(d) STORE SEAM: `commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs(input)` on SqliteEventStore :269 delegating to the core. `CommitExpectedVersionDecisionLegsInput` = {commandKind, committedResultBytes, correlationId, decidedAt, key, legs, requestBytes} — note it takes NO `targetAggregateId`: the primary aggregate comes from `legs[0]`, which its own doc states explicitly ("legs[0] is the PRIMARY leg and is the one the durable decision record describes"). `ExpectedVersionDecisionLeg` = {aggregateId, events, expectedVersion}. MAX_DECISION_LEGS is 8 and the legs module refuses over-length with a limit-exceeded code, so two legs is well inside.

(e) THE BLIND SPOT, confirmed by reading the fold: `readDurableLedger` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:133-155) does `aggregates.set(decision.targetAggregateId, ...)` and nothing else. A SECONDARY leg's aggregate never appears in the DurableLedger at all. Consequences, both binding on step 3 and on any future reader: the authority leg's fence MUST come from `store.getAggregateVersion(aggId)` and NOT from `versionOf(ledger, aggId)` — the latter would silently return 0 forever and every write after the first would be a stale-version conflict; and a reader of these bodies must go to the store's events, not the ledger.

ALSO MEASURED, because step 5 depends on both being additive:
- `commitAccepted` (:215-247) builds its own `eventDraft` (eventId `${commandId}-${eventType}`) and `decisionKey(request)` = {commandId, principalId, projectId}, and surfaces a non-EFFECTS_COMMITTED `resultCode` under DURABLE_STORE rather than reporting an accepted decision. `commitAcceptedLegs` must share all of that verbatim or the two seams diverge in exactly the place the comment at :231-235 warns about.
- `persistApprovalGate(result, prior, candidate)` (approval-gate.ts:67-81) returns the result unchanged when no gate is selected and otherwise adds ONE key, `workIdentity`. Merging my binding fields into that result is additive: `approval.decide`'s durable reader takes {state, submissionHash} BY NAME, so extra sibling keys cannot disturb it.

CAPS as they stand: bootstrap-ledger.ts 281 (pre-existing, stays under the 400 split line), planning-services.ts 214, and the new module must land <=250.

CASES: (a) accepted control in five arms — one decision (+1, counted before/after), authority aggregate at version 1, both bodies decode through the CORE decoders with NONZERO steps and obligations, the durable payload's six identity fields EQUAL the identity the core carrier sealed on PlanningSubmissionSealed, bodiesDigest equals the length-framed sha256 over both canonical byte arrays, and the decision result bytes carry {authorityRef, bodiesDigest, criteriaDigest, planHash} with the key bearing projectId + principalId. TWO PLAN CASES CHANGED, both because I measured the seam rather than assuming it.

1. THE PLAN'S "CONFLICT" ARM IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE PRODUCTION EDGE. `replayOf` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:256-278) looks the decision up by key = {commandId, principalId, projectId}, checks ONLY that commandKind matches, and returns the existing decision as a REPLAY — before any handler runs and before the store ever sees the new request bytes. So "same decision identity, conflicting command bytes" does not refuse at this edge; it REPLAYS the original, which is what DoD 3's "preserves the original bytes" actually means here. The store's own guard is real but sits beneath a short-circuit. I assert the reachable behaviour and record the unreachable one rather than writing an arm that would have to be forced.

2. THE FENCE ARM IS WORTH MORE THAN THE CONFLICT ARM, so I wrote it. `readDurableLedger` folds only `decision.targetAggregateId`, so the authority aggregate — a SECONDARY leg — never appears in the ledger. The test asserts exactly that asymmetry: `aggregates.get(authorityRef)` is UNDEFINED while `store.getAggregateVersion(authorityRef)` is 1 and the run aggregate IS in the ledger. That is the trap for every future reader, and it is why the builder must fence from the store: `versionOf(ledger, ...)` would return 0 forever and every write after the first would be a stale-version conflict. A separate builder arm asserts `leg.expectedVersion === store.getAggregateVersion(...)`.

MEASURED WHILE HERE, for step 4: the store's multi-leg path reports a stale fence on ANY leg as `resultCode: "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT"` with `effectDisposition: "NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT"` and `targetAggregateId` naming the offending leg (packages/store/src/command-decision-multi-leg.test.ts:203-207). `commitAcceptedLegs` must surface that under DURABLE_STORE exactly as `commitAccepted` does at :236-238, or the two seams diverge at the precise point that comment warns about.

BUILDER SURFACE, so refusals are reachable at all: core's fold answers body-level refusals BEFORE the daemon builder sees them on the production path, so the refusal arms address the exported builder directly — a submission hash that does not recompute (module code + layer, and ZERO residue: event count and aggregate version unchanged), a tampered body digest passing through with the CORE's own PLAN_REVISION_DIGEST_MISMATCH@PLAN_REVISION_DIGEST, and an absent member reading as the legacy arm. Wiring liveness is step 6's drill, not a claim here.

implementationPlan.note:
GREEN part 1. NEW apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-authority-persistence.ts, 220 lines by `grep -c ''` (cap 250), plus the exact one-line LF bridge. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo.

EXPORTS: `buildPlanningAuthorityLeg(input)`, `planningAuthorityAggregateId(runId)`, the closed 3-code roster, the closed layer TYPE (never the const — the security roster counts exported `*_LAYER(S)`), and the `PlanningAuthorityBinding` shape the commit seam merges into the decision result.

RESULT IS A THREE-ARM UNION, not a boolean: `{kind:"ABSENT"}` for the legacy/EXPANSION proposal, `{kind:"REFUSED", code, layer}` carrying whichever authority answered, and `{kind:"LEG", leg, binding}`. Absence and refusal are different answers and the caller must not be able to conflate them — that is the same distinction the core carrier draws between an absent member and a malformed one.

BODY ADMISSION COMPOSES THE CORE CODECS. encode -> decode -> derive, in that order, for both bodies. The encode path runs full admission internally and verifies the body's own carried digest, so a malformed or digest-inconsistent body is CORE's verdict and travels out with CORE's code and layer unchanged; the decode hands back core's own frozen record, which is what every field is read from — never the caller's object. Both digests are RECOMPUTED via derivePlanRevisionDigest / deriveAcceptanceContractDigest, so a carried digest decides nothing.

THE ONE CROSS-BIND THIS MODULE OWNS: recomputed planHash === state.submissionHash, refusing PLANNING_AUTHORITY_SUBMISSION_HASH_MISMATCH. I deliberately did NOT add comparisons of criteriaDigest/revisionId/graphRevisionRef/graphContentHash against "the sealed identity", which the plan lists: this builder derives those fields from the SAME bodies the core carrier derived them from, so such a check would compare a value with itself — a tautology that reads like a guard. The end-to-end binding is asserted where it is real: the test compares the DURABLE payload's six identity fields against the identity on the core's sealed event, which only holds if both layers admitted the same bodies.

THE FENCE. `expectedVersion: store.getAggregateVersion(authorityRef)`, never `versionOf(ledger, ...)`, with the reason in the code: `readDurableLedger` folds only `decision.targetAggregateId`, so a SECONDARY leg's aggregate is invisible to it and a ledger fence would read 0 forever — every write after the first would be a stale-version conflict. A test asserts the leg's fence equals the store's version, and another asserts the ledger genuinely cannot see the aggregate.

bodiesDigest is sha256 over the LENGTH-FRAMED concatenation of both canonical byte arrays. Without the frames, a byte moved from the end of one body to the start of the other leaves the digest unchanged; the comment says so at the function.

eventId is `${runId}-PlanningAuthorityBodiesSealed` — deterministic, unique per run, and derived from data the builder already holds. I did not key it on commandId, which is not part of the builder's input, and content-addressing it on the bodies digest would collide across two runs proposing identical bodies.

The authority member read is a plain descriptor read with an exact two-key check, and the comment states WHY that is sufficient: the member has already survived the core fold, where `planAuthorityCarry` reads the descriptor and refuses an accessor outright, so a getter shell cannot arrive here green. The exact-key check still refuses a member that is null, non-object, or carries extra keys.

implementationPlan.note:
GREEN part 2. bootstrap-ledger.ts 281 -> 334 lines (well under the 400 split line), typecheck exit 0.

(1) SERVICE_REFUSED_BY extended per its OWN precedent, and each addition has a stated reason in the file: `"PLANNING_AUTHORITY_PERSISTENCE"` spelled LITERALLY because that module keeps its layer const private (the security roster counts exported `*_LAYER(S)`), and the two BODY vocabularies SPREAD from their exported rosters — `...ACCEPTANCE_CONTRACT_LAYERS` and `...PLAN_REVISION_LAYERS` — so a core codec's verdict travels under the layer that produced it rather than under a daemon restatement. I did NOT add "PLANNING_AUTHORITY_ENVELOPE": that layer belongs to task-bb923a7b's seam and adding it here would advertise a boundary this row does not own.

THE COMPILE-TIME AGREEMENT CHECK IS REAL, not a comment. The persistence module exports a CLOSED `PlanningAuthorityRefusalLayer` = its own layer union the two core body layer types, and `proposePlan` passes `authority.layer` straight into `refuse(...)`, whose third parameter is `ServiceRefusedBy`. If a future core layer appears in a refusal without being in the roster, that call stops compiling. That is the same mechanism `recordProbe` uses for the provider pair, and it is why the union is worth naming rather than typing the field `string` — my first draft did type it `string`, which would have made the roster edit unverified.

(2) `commitAcceptedLegs(store, request, plan, extraLegs)` lands BESIDE `commitAccepted`, not in front of it. Both now delegate their accept/refuse handling to one new private `decided(request, response)`, so the two seams cannot drift on the point the existing comment warns about: a non-EFFECTS_COMMITTED `resultCode` is surfaced under DURABLE_STORE rather than reported as an accepted decision. I MOVED that comment onto `decided` and extended it with the multi-leg case — the store reports a stale fence on ANY leg the same way (measured: command-decision-multi-leg.test.ts:203-207 pins `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT` / `NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT` with `targetAggregateId` naming the offending leg).

`legs[0]` is built exactly as the single-aggregate path builds its only leg — same `eventDraft(request, plan)`, same `decisionKey(request)`, same `requestBytes` and `committedResultBytes` construction — so the decision record a reader sees has an identical shape either way. Existing single-aggregate callers are deliberately NOT rerouted: they have no second leg, and an empty `extraLegs` would add a code path that never runs.

ONE THING WORTH FLAGGING TO QA about the edit mechanics: bootstrap-ledger.ts is stored CRLF while the files I had been editing are LF, so my first patch attempt matched nothing and wrote nothing. I made the patcher match either form and write back whichever it matched, so the diff is 70 insertions / 17 deletions — localized to my edits — rather than a whole-file line-ending rewrite. `git diff --stat` confirms 87 lines touched, not 281.

THE WIRING, in `proposePlan` after `foldChain` succeeds and before any durable write:
  const authority = buildPlanningAuthorityLeg({ lastCommand: last, request, runId, state: folded.state, store });
  if (authority.kind === "REFUSED") return refuse(request.kind, authority.code, authority.layer);
Three arms, and the ORDER is the point. The builder runs BEFORE the commit, so a refusal returns with no event and no decision written — DoD 2's "before any event or decision residue" is a property of statement order here, and the builder-surface test asserts the zero residue by counting the authority aggregate's events and version after a refusal.

ABSENT keeps the existing `commitAccepted` path byte-identical: same CommitPlan, same seam, no extra key in the result. That is decision D1 — the authority member stays OPTIONAL at this edge and the mandatory flip is owned by task-47b2dbc6. Two tests pin it: the legacy chain commits with no authority aggregate at all, and its sealed event carries no `authority` key.

LEG merges the four binding fields into the `persistApprovalGate` result and commits through `commitAcceptedLegs` with the RUN leg primary and the authority leg second — ONE decision, so plan and criteria content cannot survive without `PlanProposed` nor `PlanProposed` without them (task rail 3). The merge is ADDITIVE by construction: I spread `carried` FIRST and let `state`/`submissionHash` follow, so the two names `approval.decide`'s durable reader takes cannot be shadowed by a binding field. `persistApprovalGate` itself is untouched — it either returns its input unchanged or adds one `workIdentity` key.

DoD 5 CHECKS: no new RuntimeCommandKind (nothing in packages/contracts changed); the payload vocabulary roster stays ["commands", "runId"]; no caller-selected approval authority — the only caller-supplied thing that reaches durability here is the two BODIES, and both are re-admitted and re-digested by core before anything is written.

The `last` chain element the builder reads is the same value `proposePlan` already computed for its `lastKind !== "plan.propose"` ingress guard, so the builder cannot be looking at a different command than the one the fold ended on.

Envelope suite untouched and green in meaning: this row writes a BODIES record and never calls `admitPlanningAuthorityEnvelope`, so b42db644's 45 tests neither changed nor needed to.

implementationPlan.note:
8 DRILLS, one at a time, SHA-256-verified restores. 6 RED by name. ONE was a REAL hole in my tests that I closed, and ONE is a disclosed equivalent mutant with the reason proven from the code.

THE HOLE — and it was in the very clause I said I was guarding. H6 fenced the authority leg at a CONSTANT ZERO and the whole suite stayed green (46 passed, 0 failed). My fence assertion was `leg.expectedVersion === store.getAggregateVersion(authorityRef)` measured on a store where the authority aggregate had NEVER been written, so both sides were 0 and a constant satisfied it. That is exactly the trap step 1(e) exists to prevent, and my test would not have caught the bug it was written for.
FIX: a new arm that COMMITS a proposal first (aggregate -> version 1) and only then builds, asserting `leg.expectedVersion === 1`. Re-drilled: H6 now reds on "fences a NON-EMPTY authority aggregate at its current store version", exactly one test.

THE PLAN'S FIVE, all RED:
(i) WIRING — the builder call neutered to ABSENT -> "returns the binding fields in the decision result bytes". The persistence is wired, not decorative.
(ii) ATOMICITY — `[]` passed instead of `[authority.leg]` -> SIX tests red while `PlanProposed` still lands, including "commits the bodies on a second leg of the SAME decision" and "keeps the authority aggregate invisible to the ledger but readable from the store". This is the hardest-argued clause (task rail 3) and the breadth is the point: the suite binds BOTH legs to one decision rather than checking that a commit happened.
(iii) REFUSAL LIVENESS — the builder forced to always return its cross-bind refusal -> 9 red including the builder-surface control, while the ZERO-RESIDUE assertions still PASS on the refused store. Precommit refusal genuinely leaves nothing durable.
(iv) BINDING — bodiesDigest computed over ONE body only -> "binds the bodies digest over BOTH bodies, length-framed", exactly one test.
(v) SERVER-RECOMPUTE — see below.

H5 IS A DISCLOSED EQUIVALENT MUTANT, and I first wrote it WRONG. My initial version called a function that does not exist, so the suite reddened with a ReferenceError — a red for the wrong reason, which is not a kill. Rewritten honestly as "adopt the DECODED body's carried `planHash` instead of the derivation": GREEN, 47 passed. STEP-1 MEASUREMENT — the plan's step 1(c) "Confirm folded PlanningRunState exposes ... lifecycle==='PLAN_REVIEW', sealedHashes{...}, graphRevisionRef" DOES NOT CONFIRM. It disconfirms, and that makes step 3's composition impossible rather than merely awkward. Full evidence, all measured at HEAD a287786 by running production code, not by reading it.

(1) THE FOLDED STATE AT THE END OF A plan.propose CHAIN. Drove the real `reducePlanningRun` through create_draft -> ready -> claim -> plan.propose and printed the result:

Only after a FIFTH command, planning.finalize_submission, does it become:
  AFTER_FINALIZE = { lifecycle: "PLAN_REVIEW", graphRevisionRef: "graph-1" }
`sealedHashes` and `graphRevisionRef` are written by `finalize` (planning-run-submission.ts:162-166), never by `propose`. `propose` writes only submissionHash + lifecycle (:65-69).

(2) WHAT THE ENVELOPE DEMANDS. `readSubmission` (planning-authority-envelope-contract.ts:178-196) refuses PLANNING_AUTHORITY_ENVELOPE_GATE_UNSATISFIED unless `submission.lifecycle === "PLAN_REVIEW"` (:183-185), and MALFORMED unless `sealedHashes` is four hex64 values (:189, readHashes :164-172) and `graphRevisionRef` is a nonempty bounded string (:186). Its own comment states the intent: "an unsealed run has no authority to carry, so a non-PLAN_REVIEW lifecycle is refused here rather than normalized into one."

(3) NO CHAIN CAN SATISFY BOTH. `proposePlan` requires the LAST chain element to be kind "plan.propose" (planning-services.ts:102, else BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID/DAEMON_INGRESS). A chain that reaches PLAN_REVIEW must contain finalize, after which another plan.propose is refused — measured, verbatim: {"error":{"code":"ILLEGAL_TRANSITION","details":{"aggregateKind":"PLANNING_RUN","commandKind":"plan.propose","sourceState":"PLAN_REVIEW"}}}. PLANNING_RUN_TRANSITIONS allows plan.propose only from PLANNING and SUBMISSION_DRAINING (planning-run-reducer.ts:64).

(4) THE GATE IS UNREACHABLE FROM EVERY DAEMON SEAM, not just this one. PLANNING_HANDLERS is exactly {"approval.decide", "plan.propose"} (planning-services.ts:211-214). Only proposePlan folds a caller chain; decideApproval reads a durable run and folds nothing. `grep -rn finalize_submission apps/daemon/src` outside tests returns ZERO hits.
